## `AiGovernanceKpi`

Aggregated KPI for the AI governance dashboard.

### Fields {.no_toc}

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `count` | [`Int`](scalars.md#int) | Count in the selected timeframe. |

Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Running totals across the selected timeframe: each bucket is the total as of the end of that bucket, seeded with the 30 days before the timeframe. Agents count from the bucket of their first session in that period onward, so the series is monotonic and its last point can exceed `count`. |
| `previousCount` | [`Int`](scalars.md#int) | Count in the preceding timeframe of equal length. |
| `trend` | [`[AiGovernanceKpiTrendPoint!]`](#aigovernancekpitrendpoint) | Bucketed counts across the selected timeframe. Each bucket is computed independently, so for distinct-count KPIs such as agents the buckets do not sum to `count`: an agent active on several days is counted once per day here and once in the total. |

| Name | Type | Description |

| `id` | [`ID!`](scalars.md#id) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.5.<br/><br/>Artifact Registry's UUID for the namespace mapped to the organization. Neither a GitLab namespace nor a GitLab global ID. Pass it as `resourceId` to the Artifact Registry role mutations. Present even when the status is `unknown`. |
| `slug` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Registry slug, Artifact Registry's immutable identifier for the namespace. `null` when the status is `unknown`. |
| `statistics` | [`ArtifactRegistryNamespaceStatistics`](#artifactregistrynamespacestatistics) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.5.<br/><br/>Namespace-wide Artifact Registry statistics, read as the current user when this field is selected. `null` on any unresolved read, so an unavailable service or a drifted slug omits the figures rather than raising. The parent field returns `null` when the `artifact_registry_ui` feature flag is disabled, so this field is not reached. |
| `status` | [`String!`](scalars.md#string) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Status Artifact Registry returned, one of `active`, `suspended`, `disabled`, `blocked`, `deleted`, or `purged`, or `unknown` when the mapped namespace did not resolve. Deliberately a string rather than an enum so a status Artifact Registry adds within its API version reaches the response instead of raising. |
| `userPermissions` | [`ArtifactRegistryNamespacePermissions!`](#artifactregistrynamespacepermissions) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.5.<br/><br/>Permissions Artifact Registry grants the current user on the namespace, read from the namespace details as the user when this field is selected. Advisory, because Artifact Registry authorizes every request on its own. Every permission is `false` when Artifact Registry returned no verdicts. The parent field returns `null` when the `artifact_registry_ui` feature flag is disabled, so this block is not reached. |

| `osVariant` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.5.<br/><br/>CPU variant an image manifest targets. Null on an index, on most images, and always null on a remote repository. |

## `ContainerProtectionRepositoryRule`

A container repository protection rule designed to prevent users with a certain access level or lower from altering the container registry.

### Fields {.no_toc}

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `id` | [`ContainerRegistryProtectionRuleID!`](scalars.md#containerregistryprotectionruleid) | ID of the container repository protection rule. |
| `minimumAccessLevelForDelete` | [`ContainerProtectionRepositoryRuleAccessLevel`](enums.md#containerprotectionrepositoryruleaccesslevel) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 17.11.<br/><br/>Minimum GitLab access level required to delete container images from the container repository. Valid values include `MAINTAINER`, `OWNER`, or `ADMIN`. If the value is `nil`, the default minimum access level is `DEVELOPER`. Valid only when feature flag `container_registry_protected_containers_delete` is enabled. |
| `minimumAccessLevelForPush` | [`ContainerProtectionRepositoryRuleAccessLevel`](enums.md#containerprotectionrepositoryruleaccesslevel) | Minimum GitLab access level required to push container images to the container repository. Valid values include `MAINTAINER`, `OWNER`, or `ADMIN`. If the value is `nil`, the default minimum access level is `DEVELOPER`. |
| `repositoryPathPattern` | [`String!`](scalars.md#string) | Container repository path pattern protected by the protection rule. Must start with the project's full path. For example: `my-project/*-prod-*`. Wildcard character `*` is allowed anywhere after the project's full path. |

## `DuoWorkflowEvent`

Events that describe the history and progress of a GitLab Duo Agent Platform session.

### Fields {.no_toc}

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `checkpoint` | [`JsonString`](scalars.md#jsonstring) | Deprecated in GitLab 18.7. Checkpoints are big & contain internal langgraph details. |
| `checkpointNs` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.3.<br/><br/>LangGraph checkpoint namespace this checkpoint belongs to. Blank for the session's own top-level checkpoint lineage; this field only ever surfaces that lineage (via first_checkpoint/latest_checkpoint), never a nested subgraph invocation's own. |
| `checkpointWrites` | [`[DuoWorkflowCheckpointWrite!]`](#duoworkflowcheckpointwrite) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.3.<br/><br/>Pending writes associated with the checkpoint, e.g. interrupts awaiting resumption. |
| `compressedCheckpoint` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Checkpoint of the event, zlib-compressed and Base64-encoded. |
| `currentThread` | [`Int!`](scalars.md#int) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Compaction group this checkpoint belongs to. The writer bumps it on every compaction and resets it when its process restarts, so a client that resumes a session must read it back from here to keep numbering the groups correctly. |
| `duoMessages` | [`[DuoMessage!]`](#duomessage) | Messages from the ui_chat_log for the checkpoint. |
| `errors` | [`[String!]`](scalars.md#string) | Message errors. |
| `executionStatus` | [`String!`](scalars.md#string) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 17.10.<br/><br/>Granular status of the session's execution. |
| `lastDuoMessage` | [`DuoMessage`](#duomessage) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.3.<br/><br/>Most recent message from the ui_chat_log for the checkpoint. Cheaper than duoMessages for list previews: it reads only the latest message instead of the full chat log. |
| `metadata` | [`JsonString`](scalars.md#jsonstring) | Metadata associated with the event. |
| `parentTs` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | UUID v7 timestamp identifier of the parent message for branched conversations or responses. |
| `threadTs` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | UUID v7 timestamp identifier for the conversation thread/session in LangGraph state management. |
| `workflowDefinition` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | GitLab Duo Agent Platform flow type based on its capabilities. |
| `workflowGoal` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Goal of the session. |
| `workflowStatus` | [`DuoWorkflowStatus`](enums.md#duoworkflowstatus) | Status of the session. |

| `theirPath` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Path of the conflicting file on the target branch. |

Defaults to `[TITLE, DESCRIPTION]`. Requires the `search` argument.'.</dd><dt>`includeAncestors` ([`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean))</dt><dd>Include work items from ancestor groups. Ignored for project namespaces.</dd><dt>`includeArchived` ([`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 18.5.<br/><br/>Return work items from archived projects. Ignored for project namespaces.</dd><dt>`includeDescendantWorkItems` ([`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 18.3.<br/><br/>Whether to include work items of descendant parents when filtering by parent_ids.</dd><dt>`includeDescendants` ([`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean))</dt><dd>Include work items from descendant groups and projects. Ignored for project namespaces.</dd><dt>`iterationCadenceId` ([`[IterationsCadenceID!]`](scalars.md#iterationscadenceid))</dt><dd>Filter by a list of iteration cadence IDs (maximum is 100 IDs).</dd><dt>`iterationId` ([`[ID]`](scalars.md#id))</dt><dd>List of iteration Global IDs applied to the issue (maximum is 100 IDs).</dd><dt>`iterationWildcardId` ([`IterationWildcardId`](enums.md#iterationwildcardid))</dt><dd>Filter by iteration ID wildcard.</dd><dt>`labelName` ([`[String!]`](scalars.md#string))</dt><dd>Labels applied to the work item (maximum is 100 labels).</dd><dt>`milestoneTitle` ([`[String!]`](scalars.md#string))</dt><dd>Milestone applied to the work item (maximum is 100 milestones).</dd><dt>`milestoneWildcardId` ([`MilestoneWildcardId`](enums.md#milestonewildcardid))</dt><dd>Filter by milestone ID wildcard. Incompatible with `milestoneTitle`.</dd><dt>`myReactionEmoji` ([`String`](scalars.md#string))</dt><dd>Filter by reaction emoji applied by the current user. Wildcard values `NONE` and `ANY` are supported.</dd><dt>`not` ([`NegatedWorkItemFilterInput`](input_objects.md#negatedworkitemfilterinput))</dt><dd>Negated work item arguments.</dd><dt>`or` ([`UnionedWorkItemFilterInput`](input_objects.md#unionedworkitemfilterinput))</dt><dd>List of arguments with inclusive `OR`.</dd><dt>`parentIds` ([`[WorkItemID!]`](scalars.md#workitemid))</dt><dd>Filter work items by global IDs of their parent items (maximum is 100 IDs).</dd><dt>`parentWildcardId` ([`WorkItemParentWildcardId`](enums.md#workitemparentwildcardid))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 18.5.<br/><br/>Filter by parent ID wildcard. Incompatible with parentIds.</dd><dt>`releaseTag` ([`[String!]`](scalars.md#string))</dt><dd>Release tag associated with the work item's milestone (maximum is 100 tags). Ignored when parent is a group.</dd><dt>`releaseTagWildcardId` ([`ReleaseTagWildcardId`](enums.md#releasetagwildcardid))</dt><dd>Filter by release tag wildcard.</dd><dt>`requirementLegacyWidget` ([`RequirementLegacyFilterInput`](input_objects.md#requirementlegacyfilterinput))</dt><dd>Deprecated in GitLab 15.9. Use work item IID filter instead.</dd><dt>`search` ([`String`](scalars.md#string))</dt><dd>Search query for title or description.</dd><dt>`sort` ([`WorkItemSort`](enums.md#workitemsort))</dt><dd>Sort work items by criteria.</dd><dt>`state` ([`IssuableState`](enums.md#issuablestate))</dt><dd>Current state of the work item.</dd><dt>`status` ([`WorkItemWidgetStatusFilterInput`](input_objects.md#workitemwidgetstatusfilterinput))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 18.0.<br/><br/>Filter by status.</dd><dt>`subscribed` ([`SubscriptionStatus`](enums.md#subscriptionstatus))</dt><dd>Work items the current user is subscribed to.</dd><dt>`timeframe` ([`Timeframe`](input_objects.md#timeframe))</dt><dd>List items overlapping the given timeframe. Ignored for project namespaces.</dd><dt>`types` ([`[IssueType!]`](enums.md#issuetype))</dt><dd>Filter work items by the given work item types.</dd><dt>`updatedAfter` ([`Time`](scalars.md#time))</dt><dd>Work items updated after the timestamp.</dd><dt>`updatedBefore` ([`Time`](scalars.md#time))</dt><dd>Work items updated before the timestamp.</dd><dt>`verificationStatusWidget` ([`VerificationStatusFilterInput`](input_objects.md#verificationstatusfilterinput))</dt><dd>Input for verification status widget filter.</dd><dt>`weight` ([`String`](scalars.md#string))</dt><dd>Weight applied to the work item, "none" and "any" values are supported.</dd><dt>`weightWildcardId` ([`WeightWildcardId`](enums.md#weightwildcardid))</dt><dd>Filter by weight ID wildcard. Incompatible with weight.</dd><dt>`workItemTypeIds` ([`[WorkItemsTypeID!]`](scalars.md#workitemstypeid))</dt><dd>Filter work items by work item type global IDs.</dd></dl> |

The `ids` argument cannot be combined with pagination arguments. Returns `null` when the current user cannot read the policies of the container. This field is a [connection](#connections-and-pagination) and accepts the four standard pagination arguments: `before`, `after`, `first`, `last`. <br><br> <strong>Arguments for `policies`:</strong> <dl><dt>`ids` ([`[Int!]`](scalars.md#int))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Maximum is 1000 IDs.</dd><dt>`triggerType` ([`String`](scalars.md#string))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Return only the policies that respond to this trigger. Valid values are the ids in the policy store triggers catalog.</dd></dl> |
| `policyEvaluations` | [`GovernPolicyEvaluationConnection`](#governpolicyevaluationconnection) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Recorded evaluations of the policies stored in the policy store for the organization or group, newest first. This field is a [connection](#connections-and-pagination) and accepts the four standard pagination arguments: `before`, `after`, `first`, `last`. <br><br> <strong>Arguments for `policyEvaluations`:</strong> <dl><dt>`evaluatedAfter` ([`Time`](scalars.md#time))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Return only the evaluations that ran at or after the given timestamp.</dd><dt>`evaluatedBefore` ([`Time`](scalars.md#time))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Return only the evaluations that ran at or before the given timestamp.</dd><dt>`mode` ([`GovernPolicyEvaluationMode`](enums.md#governpolicyevaluationmode))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Return only the evaluations that ran in the given enforcement mode.</dd><dt>`policyId` ([`Int`](scalars.md#int))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Return only the evaluations of the policy with the given ID.</dd><dt>`verdict` ([`GovernPolicyEvaluationVerdict`](enums.md#governpolicyevaluationverdict))</dt><dd>Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 19.4.<br/><br/>Return only the evaluations that produced the given verdict.</dd></dl> |

### Fields {.no_toc}

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `crossProjectPushForJobTokenAllowed` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Indicates the ability to push to this repository using a job token from an allowlisted project. |
| `displayPipelineVariables` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Indicates whether pipeline variables can be displayed in the UI. |
| `groupRunnersEnabled` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Indicates whether group runners are enabled for the project. |
| `inboundJobTokenScopeEnabled` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Indicates whether CI/CD job tokens generated in other projects have restricted access to this project. |
| `jobTokenScopeEnabled` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Indicates whether CI/CD job tokens generated in this project have restricted access to other projects. |
| `keepLatestArtifact` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Indicates whether the latest artifact should be kept for the project. |
| `maxPipelinesPerMergeTrain` | [`Int`](scalars.md#int) | Maximum number of parallel pipelines per merge train. When null, the plan limit applies. |
| `mergePipelinesEnabled` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Indicates whether merged results pipelines are enabled. |
| `mergeTrainEnforcement` | [`MergeTrainEnforcement!`](enums.md#mergetrainenforcement) | Merge train enforcement level for the project. |
| `mergeTrainsEnabled` | [`Boolean`](scalars.md#boolean) | Whether merge trains are enabled. |

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

Introduced in GitLab 18.11.<br/><br/>Restriction on the source of write requests. `ANYWHERE` allows all sources, `CI_ONLY` requires a CI job token, `CI_ON_PROTECTED_BRANCH_ONLY` requires a CI job on a protected branch. |
| `id` | [`TerraformStateProtectionRuleID!`](scalars.md#terraformstateprotectionruleid) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 18.11.<br/><br/>Global ID of the Terraform state protection rule. |

Introduced in GitLab 18.11.<br/><br/>Minimum GitLab access level required to perform write operations on the Terraform state. Valid values include `DEVELOPER`, `MAINTAINER`, `OWNER`, or `ADMIN`. |
| `stateName` | [`String!`](scalars.md#string) | Status: Experiment. Introduced in GitLab 18.11.<br/><br/>Terraform state name protected by the rule. |

## `UserCoreConnection`

## Connections and pagination

Some fields return a _connection_: a paginated list of items that follows the
[Relay cursor connections specification](https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm).
Because every connection shares the same pagination fields and arguments, they are
documented here once rather than repeated for every connection field.

### Standard connection fields

Every connection type has the following fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| `nodes` | `[Item]` | The items in the current page. The item type depends on the connection. |
| `edges` | `[Edge]` | The edges. Each edge wraps a `node` and a `cursor`. |
| `pageInfo` | [`PageInfo!`](objects.md#pageinfo) | Pagination information. |

Every edge type has the following fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| `node` | `Item` | The item at the end of the edge. The item type depends on the connection. |
| `cursor` | [`String!`](scalars.md#string) | A cursor for use in pagination. |

Some connections and edges have additional fields specific to their type.
These are documented individually in each connection or edge section above.

### Pagination arguments

All connection fields accept the following optional pagination arguments:

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `after` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Returns the items that come after the specified cursor. |
| `before` | [`String`](scalars.md#string) | Returns the items that come before the specified cursor. |
| `first` | [`Int`](scalars.md#int) | Returns the first _n_ items from the list. |
| `last` | [`Int`](scalars.md#int) | Returns the last _n_ items from the list. |

### Querying a connection

The following example queries the `projects` field, which returns a
[`ProjectConnection`](objects.md#projectconnection). It shows the pagination arguments in use
and annotates each part of the response with its type:

```graphql
{
  projects(
    first: 10        # optional - return at most 10 items
    after: "abc123"  # optional - start after this cursor (from a previous endCursor)
  ) {                # ProjectConnection
    pageInfo {       # PageInfo
      hasNextPage    # Boolean - true if more pages follow
      endCursor      # String - pass as `after:` to fetch the next page
    }
    nodes {          # [Project] - the items on this page
      id
      name
    }
    edges {          # [ProjectEdge] - the same items, each with a cursor
      cursor         # String - cursor for this specific item
      node {         # Project
        id
        name
      }
    }
  }
}
```

To fetch the next page, pass the `endCursor` value from `pageInfo` as the `after` argument.
Use `last` and `before` to paginate in reverse.
